text: UPDATED REVIEW Talk about a location that just keeps getting better with age; in the 9 months since my first review the Lambertville OwowCow has seen a marked improvement in staff, an increase in options, and the ever-high-quality ice cream I have come to know and love is still amazing. PROS The ice cream is the reason you come to OwowCow. It is thick, rich, and flavorful. There is always a rotating blend of wonderful and creative flavors, ranging from traditional (three variants on vanilla and the classic "I Hate Chocolate" - the best chocolate ice cream you may ever taste) to unique, fruity, and floral. Even better, unlike some ice cream places I have been, they have no problem with you taking your time to decide - offering samples of as many flavors as you would like and taking the time to explain what is unique about the flavors. The serving sizes here are VERY generous. In a regular cup (my normal order) you get two giant scoops (of one or two flavors). Even for someone who loves ice cream and can eat a lot, I am always completely satisfied. They have a lot of other options besides just ice cream in a cup (although I rarely can bring myself to stray from my favorite). From shakes and floats (made with local sodas) to hand-made ice cream sandwiches (with cookies from a local baker), there is always something new to try. Also, during holidays they often have specialty cakes and pies available for order. We got their pumpkin ice cream pie over Thanksgiving - it was stunning! The staff are almost all very welcoming and friendly. When it is really busy, sometimes the staff are a little less chipper - but I would be too! It is nice to be welcomed with a smile. The location and ambiance is great. There are almost always enough seats if you want to stay and enjoy your deliciousness, the art on the walls is inviting, and it is close enough to downtown Lambertville that you can (if the weather is nice) walk downtown and enjoy the shops and then get ice cream on your way back to your car. CONS It is true that they are not the cheapest option in the world (a regular ice cream is $4.20), but they are in line with other places in the area of similar quality (and you get more bang for your buck compared to a high-end place like the Bent Spoon in Princeton). For me, the price isn't out of line, but we can't afford to come here every day either. And that's ok both for my wallet and my health. On a busy day parking can be tough, but usually workable. OVERALL OwowCow has become my favorite ice cream place in the whole region; enough so that my family and I will often make the half-hour or so drive from Princeton just for ice cream. All you really need to know is that the ice cream is fresh and delicious. Still on the fence? Come give it a try for yourself!

text: The fitness options in the Fairmount/Spring Garden area are pretty slim, so I'm really happy to have a hot yoga studio this close to my apartment! At this point, I've only attended two classes with two different instructors (Richard and Liz), but I anticipate on returning to Priya a lot more in the future. The studio itself is very open and has a lot of seating and storage space. They also have a cooler with different drinks and healthy snacks if you're feeling hungry post-yoga. Both instructors I've had class with were definitely more challenging than most yoga instructors I've experienced at other studios which I love. They do, however, provide a good range of modifications for people like me who are not as advanced in their yoga practice. There are some tolerable negatives, but they're definitely worth noting. First, there's no mirror in the studio. I could see that being a positive for some, but I like to see that my body is actually doing what it's supposed to through some of the poses. Second, the heat comes from the ceiling, and if you don't pay attention to where you place your mat, your hot yoga class will be especially hot with the heated air blasting at you. And third, both classes I've attended (7:15 pm classes) have been PACKED. Priya has tape marks to etch where mats should be placed, and there are barely a few inches between where each of the mats are on the ground. This makes it more difficult to do some of the poses that require more space, and you'll definitely end up bumping sweaty limbs with your neighbor. All-in-all, Priya's instruction seems to be above average, AND it's located so close to where I live. That's a win in my book.

Knowing that I have a car that requires a bit of extra work (I have two dogs and a 5 year old child!), I also tip the workers very generously - today it was $9. I cannot figure out if it's due to poor workmanship or the fact that certain areas are covered under a roof which makes it harder to see. But when I purchase a $30 car wash I expect to get out into the sun and not see dust covering my entire dashboard. Yes, the wash that I purchased does have a five-day clean car guarantee and I could very well take my vehicle back, complain, and have everything corrected. And yes, I have done this multiple times. The point being that I shouldn't have to have my car serviced twice because it's not done correctly the first time. Unfortunately for me, I am not the type of person who complains and therefore I will take my vehicle home and clean the interior myself. What I can do however is recommend that anyone in the South County area save their money and take your vehicle somewhere else to be washed or detailed. To be fair I will say the staff is extremely courteous and the outside of my car always looks perfect. The problem always lies in the cleaning of the interior. For these two reasons, I've given Concord Car was 2 stars.
label: NEG

text: My friends and I were lucky enough to be the only ones who booked the walking food and history tour with Dr. Gumbo yesterday so we had a really intimate party of five. Our first stop was Sobou where we tried 2 dishes- gulf shrimp and tasso ham skewer and sweet potato & duck beignets. The shrimp was really flavorful and grilled with just the right amount of crisp. The sweet potato and duck beignets were a really great blend of savory and sweet. Our second stop was Leah's Pralines where we tried their creole praline and bacon pecan brittle. Both of these were a miss for me. The praline was way too sweet and I barely tasted the bacon in the brittle. Also not really a fan of stick to your teeth sweets. Our third stop was Little Vic's where we had their muffuletta which is a Sicilian type of sandwich. Normally, I'm not a fan of deli meat but the spices that they use were quite tasty and I also really enjoyed the crunchy ciabatta bread. Our fourth stop was NOLA Po Boys where we had their catfish po boy. I thought the po boy was good but coming from CA where we have sandwich shops galore and also banh mi's by the dozens, I wasn't that impressed with the catfish po boy. Our fifth stop was Sugar & Spice Praline and Hot Sauce Bar where we were able to try as many different hot sauces we wanted. This is not really special to the tour because any customer can sample this establishment's sauces. Still can't complain that this was a stop because I'm a hot sauce lover through and through. Our sixth stop was Tujague's where we tried their slow cooked beef brisket. This was really tasty and super tender. I'm not a big meat eater but I thoroughly enjoyed the beef brisket. I forgot the name of our last stop where we had the gumbo and I'm probably not the most objective person to rate gumbo because I personally don't like the idea of putting rice in my soup and letting it get to that mushy consistency. I also didn't really like the flavor of the gumbo so this was also a miss for me. Overall, I would recommend. The stops are diverse enough that you get a good idea of New Orleans food. Dr. Gumbo does manage to weave in history throughout the tastings. My only main complaint would be that he should probably work in more history/stories during the walking portion of the tour. I've done a handful of walking food tours and the guides are usually talking and walking at the same time keeping the group entertained. However, through a considerable portion of the walking, we just found ourselves following Dr. Gumbo. I found myself having to ask questions to stay engaged and just to satisfy my general curiosity.

text: This is a huge convenience to have in the downtown area, especially after being used to doing all of my shopping at the Marsh on New Jersey. This is a full sized grocery store. It has just about everything you could be looking for and a lot more. One of my favorite things in this place is their large variety of pay-by-the-pound options for dried fruit, nuts, trail mix, beans, grains, oat, and a variety of other items. I'm guessing they have 80 or so containers that are filled with these items that you can then take as much or little as you need and it is paid for by weight. They also have a great selection of wines, beer, and cheeses. The deli is large and has plenty of meats and cheeses, as well as specialty items and prepared dishes. They even have some olive bar selections. Like you would expect from a grocery store downtown, they are more expensive then stores selling the same thing out in the suburbs, but the convenience makes it worth it. They have a garage with free parking for customers (make sure to get a voucher at checkout), so you can stay out of the rain getting to and from your car. They also have a decent amount of bike parking both outside of the store and inside the garage. It isn't located on the cultural trail, but it is only a short detour from that, and Michigan Road actually has a bike lane that I usually take over here. They do a good job of stocking shelves, which is also a significant difference from the other downtown Marsh. They have quite a few organic options in their veggie and fruit area, and they have a wide variety of offerings. I feel confident that they will always have what I am looking for, although the quality of their offerings for fresh items can be hit and miss, especially with veggies. I also think that their meat selection is often smaller than I would expect for this size store, so hopefully that eventually changes. I haven't ever been specifically for this reason, but they do have a lot of options for the lunch crowd. Their deli area makes a lot of hot foods, and they have a good sized seating area to enjoy lunch. While I will still drive down to Aldi to save some money on basic foodstuffs, this is the store I will continue to visit for a variety of items that I can't get elsewhere in the downtown area or just want the convenience of walking or biking over to the store.

The place feels cramped, and we felt like the crew was watching us the whole time. It did not make us want to shop; it made us want to leave. text: Rarely will I ever crave food from my home country but once in a while I do and when the craving hits, I come here to make some necessary purchases. I buy my lumpia wrappers here so I can make some lumpia at home. Among my regular purchases from the store are some chips, noodles, canned things from the Philippines which are very unhealthy but they do give me a lot of nostalgic feeling about living there as a child. They also carry my favorite ice cream by Magnolia (ube flavor) and some frozen siopao -- steamed bun with meat filling (I prefer pork because that is what I am used to but they do carry some wild varities, too!) While in the store, I normally browse through all the other aisles as well to see if there's anything interesting I might want to try. Lately, I have been on a mission to find these milk chocolate shaped in miniature bottles filled with vodka because a coworker of mine told me all about it. I successfully found them at the store today. I bought a box as a surprise for when I see him tomorrow! He can have them after work hours, of course. This store somewhat lacks organization in certain ways (some products are placed at random location, etc) but I like coming here. The aisles are organized by country of origin for the products which is nice. I can normally just look up at the hanging flags and decide if I need something in that aisle or not. It's a small enough store that I wouldn't mind going all the way to the other end if I want to check something out over there but it can get a little cramped if you go in at a busy time. Employees are nice during checkout and prices are reasonable so I will always come back here for my international grocery needs.

text: I literally haven't gotten my hair cut in a salon since college (a disastrous experience at a salon off Buford Highway in Atlanta where the stylist actually summoned the other stylists over mid-cut to gawk at how strangely atypical my hair was). I'm Taiwanese with super thick, super coarse, semi-wavy/curly hair, and people have never known what to do with my locks, so even though I'm by no means trained or sophisticated with hair-cuttery at all, I've always cut my own because I figured at least I know how it behaves and it saved the time/money/trouble of going in and having someone else botch up my hair. I was deeply distrustful because I feel like I have very misunderstood special-unicorn hair that nobody else gets. Essentially the fact that I actually went in to get a haircut at Bobby Mack after about seven or eight years of hacking it on my own should tell you something about their talent. I had considered several salons in Center City but was never sold enough on their work to go in. The pictures here convinced me that maybe I did need to go in so that they could fix my own handiwork and give me the foundation for a good haircut that I could grow into. Erin M cut my hair and she was just wonderful! I felt like she got the situation immediately. I explained that I needed to blend in my grown-out bangs more, and also that I needed to remove bulk at the bottom. text: The High Level Bridge is the iconic bridge of Edmonton. It was built by the CPR and opened in 1913 joining the Cities of Edmonton and Strathcona. From its onset the bridge was designed to accommodate railcars, streetcars, pedestrians and automobiles. The Edmonton Radial Railway operates the Streetcar during the summer months and it is a cheap ride to take to get from Old Strathcona to Downtown, with an amazing view as you cross the river. Often the bridge is depicted in artwork of the City because it is that iconic bridge of our City. So if you ever visit our City one thing you should try to do in the summer (May-Oct) is ride the streetcar and experience this bridge and our City from a fantastic viewpoint.

text: LUXURY APARTMENT?? I think not. In October of 2014, my fiancée accepted employment with a Nashville Hospital. I would stay behind in Michigan until Christmas. We were in scramble mode to find housing, and settled on Monthaven Park, only because they had a 3 bedroom available. We agreed to their terms sight unseen. The base rent was $1190, but because we had bicycles, and they had no bike racks, we were forced to rent a storage locker for an additional $40/month. In Michigan, we were renting a second floor flat, six rooms total, shared basement, paid water for $750/month. When I asked why the rent was so high at Monthaven, I was told, "Sir...this is a Luxury Apartment." With that statement, my expectations were set. When we arrived in mid-October, we signed papers and were taken to our unit, a second floor 3 bedroom, 2 bath. We did a walk through to assess the condition of the unit. We pointed out several faults in various places, including deep gouges in the floor in the kitchen and bathroom. We were promised a repair. The lady also pointed out the new stove and refrigerator. We went grocery shopping and came home to make a pizza. It was then that we noticed that our 'new' luxury oven was so cheap, that it did not even have an oven timer. Neither of us had ever seen such a cheaply made stove/oven. Also, the new refrigerator constantly freezes the food no matter where we set the thermostat. Luxury. The floors were never repaired. Luxury. I had to get a Commercial Driver License in Tennessee. I had every necessary document except a notarized copy of a letter from the Management Company at Monthaven saying that I had a valid lease, or a notarized copy of the lease. The Management team would not help in this regard. They stated corporate policy prohibited them from notarizing anything. I advised them that this was the only missing piece to get my license. "Sorry." So after a 2 week delay and great efforts on my part, I was able to acquire another document from Michigan, which the state reluctantly accepted. Luxury. Our next purchase was a plunger. It is used almost every day. Luxury. When winter passed and springtime arrived, our 5 year old was excited to use the playgrounds on the property. They were often muddy and wet. And even better, some days we arrived to find broken beer bottles in the play area. We would come back days later, and the glass was still there and the slides were water-soaked and not useable. Luxury. Every day, we would use our little porch/balcony to enjoy coffee in the morning or a glass of wine in the evening. More than once, we would find ashes and cigarette butts on our porch (and we are not smokers). I sent emails about this and never had any response. (I found out later that some emails go to corporate, where they disappear). Luxury. Let's talk about wildlife...specifically insects. Several times we had swarms of those tiny sweet ants. We would spray and I bought ant traps. Please note that we are charged every month for pest control. One evening when we were in bed reading, a large black ant crossed the bed right over the top of us. The other night, our little boy screamed in fear. It was a giant spider that had terrorized him. Just today (9/22) we discovered a large roach under our sink. So if we are paying for pest control...what pests are we controlling?? If they are spraying for elephants...it's working. Luxury. In our unit, the master bedroom is on the wall adjacent to the exterior stairway. The stairs are deteriorating and dirty, and built on a steel frame. When people come down from the third level, especially if they do so hurriedly, our room vibrates so badly, that the globes on the ceiling fan rattle loudly enough to wake us from sleep. Just last week, a new tenant moved in to their apartment on the third floor. Sadly, it began on a Thursday evening at 11 p.m. Luxury. The swimming pools are lovely. But the chairs and umbrellas are falling apart and are torn. The tables are often so filthy, that we would not bring food or treats to enjoy poolside. We watched some people hit the ground as a chair would collapse. There were also times when we would find piles of cigarette butts at the edge of the pool. Luxury. For that amount of rent, we are also charged separately for trash, water, pest control and even we are charged for them to send our monthly rent invoice via email. Luxury. To their credit, the grounds are amazing. Flowers, trees, shrubs, grass...all lovely. Sadly, this is window dressing. Kudos to the maintenance staff. They are friendly and efficient. To say that this apartment complex is average...is a stretch. Definitely not Luxury! I will admit that we are not ones to constantly call to complain. If we did, maintenance and pest control would be here frequently. But if you are going to rent here...be prepared. Go to the hardware store. Buy ant traps, bug spray, an oven timer, and a plunger.

text: I stayed at this hotel for Metrocon June 11th-14th, so keep in mind, the hotel was busy dealing with a mass of young adults in costume. With that being said, there were still some issues that can't be overlooked or attributed to the business of a convention. First off, the hotel is very old, and that can't be helped. However, they definitely need to do some renovations if they plan on staying in business. We arrived at our room with a mass of bags including some with food. I had called ahead the week before and was assured we were already assigned to a room with a fridge. But when we got there, there was no fridge and we had to move all our stuff to another room. We forgave that but late ran into problems with the drain in the shower. The water wouldn't drain and we had to call someone to come fix it. Several times we requested more towels and never received them. The shuttle service was either terrible or really good depending on the situation. It's a free service and shouldn't be counted on, however, they knew they were a host hotel for the con and still didn't add more shuttles. I found that a little irresponsible with 3 shuttles sitting unused and a mass of people waiting. We waited to be picked up for an hour in the rain before they promised to send a cab and pay the fare (never happened). The pool was essentially a hole in the ground. The water smelt odd and stagnant, like a dirty puddle on a hot day. There is no shade, just chairs around the pool. There's nothing besides a hole in the ground, really. Don't even get me started on the hotel restaurant. The name is "Waterworks" which gave me the impression that it was poolside but it's not. There's no reason for it to be called that. Every one of our meals was disappointing. The salad is $10 and is 4 pieces of uncut lettuce leaves with dressing. Everything was soggy, strangely. How do you make a salad soggy? I don't know but they did it. The room seemed clean enough. No problems there. They have wifi...technically. It's so bad it's basically no wifi. Don't count on using the internet. Basically, if you're staying here 1 night, it's fine. Any longer, look elsewhere. Painfully average overall. Would be 3 stars but the service knocks it down to two. One positive is it's pretty cheap so if you're on a budget, this is a good place to consider. It's not too dumpy, just pretty bad service.

text: As a huge supporter of local businesses, very seldom do I leave negative reviews; however, based on my experience at Coyote Crossing last Friday evening, I feel inclined to provide feedback. While the new decor is nice, quality of food and service have been sacrificed. As a long-time former resident of Conshohocken and self-proclaimed foodie, we have dined at Coyote Crossing 25+ times over the past 18 years. We've celebrated graduations, first dates, birthdays, engagements (you get the point) dining here. We've brought out-of-town friends and family on many occasions to have the 'meal of their life.' Last Friday, we gathered three other couples to celebrate my birthday; touting that Coyote Crossing would be a place they love. Upon arrival, we entered the 'foyer' area where a male server was loudly and profanely speaking to the older, blonde woman (who I assume manages the front of the house while the owner, Carlos saunters around the restaurant/bar area). The server was furious about a group of people wanting separate checks, post-delivery of the bill. Okay, definitely an inconvenience; but, take the drama elsewhere. We then entered the bar area and ordered over-priced watered down margaritas (Note: historically, margaritas were the establishment's wheelhouse) while waiting for the rest of our group to arrive. We were promptly seated upon their arrival and not given a hard time as they were running late... that, I definitely appreciated. Once seated, we ordered several appetizers; but, yet, the server kept pushing some sampler plate and wouldn't take "no" for an answer. I get it, the staff is probably told to push the dish; but, the sales pitch made us uncomfortable. Especially after already ordering 5+ appetizers. To sum up the rest of the dinner, we had to beg for a first round of water and then the glasses were never refilled through the entire meal. Overall, the food was HORRIBLE. The tampiquena used to be a menu "special" addition and now it's a menu standard (and $9 higher than before). The meat was either undercooked/overcooked, the enchiladas were flavorless and the accompanying rice and beans were mush. The shrimp smelled/tasted entirely too fishy and the texture was sinewy. The tortilla chips were cold and chewy and there was a hair in the pico de gallo. Even the presentation of the meal has gone from classy (there used to be a cool leaf beneath the tampiquena) to resemble that of a cafeteria. I could go on an on... The bill for seven adults (each only had 1 or 2 drinks), including tip was $450. We could have saved $300 and eaten a better meal at one of the local pubs on Fayette Street. Carlos and Coyote Crossing Management....I urge you to stick to what you know and put passionate people back in the kitchen as well as the bar. For business sake, I hope expansion of the indoor bar doesn't decrease business on the once fun, now teeny-tiny outdoor area. Good luck.

No easy access AC sockets for cell phone and laptop charging - had to crawl under a desk to find them, most lights must be individually operated, no master light controls. The practice appears more about saving money for the hotel than helping to save the environment - it does not provide the minimal expected level of service to guests. At check out, they apologized and mentioned the internet was actually free for my room, yet after entering my room number on their website, it still listed the $10/night option. I ended up with over $150 in additional data charges on my cell phone since my carrier is outside the country - thanks Westin! On the positive side, the breakfasts were excellent, but pricey. They do have underground parking for $29/night which is very convenient, albeit, one can park across the street at the Library for a fraction of the cost. That said, this hotel really pushed many of my frustration buttons, resulting in a poor overall experience. Staff is very nice and friendly, but appear poorly trained and are not 100% knowledgeable. text: Is it too soon to come back? I hadn't even finished my meal when I was already thinking about scheduling my next visit to Amada. I recently went to dinner at Amada for restaurant week. My last visit had probably been a good 4 or so years prior. I won't let that gap happen again. According to a recent article, Amada was mentioned as one of the better places in Philly to go for restaurant week. I'd agree with that. In terms price, my meal would have cost $54 had it not been restaurant week. In terms of value, it really was priceless. We were able to select two items for the first and second courses, then one dessert. Some of my party also split a pitcher of the Temporada sangria for an additional fee. Here's a little rundown of my meal: First Course- Ensalada Verde: What's not to love about avocado, asparagus, favas and greens? Add a nice light dressing and a little shaved cheese and you have a great salad. Not to mention, the salad portion was pretty decent for a tapa. Escalivada: This tapa was served on two little pieces of toast and satiated my love of roasted pepers, eggplant, goat cheese, tomatoes and onions. This was small, yet tasty. I would have liked to see all of the veggies mixed together before being placed on the crostini; they were pretty segregated. Second Course- Gambas Con Garbanzos: This was hands down the best part of my meal. To think I ordered it as a last minute decision! (I was going to go with the Queso De Cabra. I really remind myself of a vegetarian sometimes). Garbanzo bean puree should find a way to be mixed into every flatbread/pizza sauce. It took the flavor to the next level. The chorizo was thinly sliced like pepperoni and added a great salty flavor. There was a piece of shrimp on each piece of flatbread. I wouldn't order it just because you want a shrimp dish. I'd order it again because I want this delicious flatbread that happens to have shrimp on it. This was a nice sized portion compared to traditional tapas. Panceta: The cauliflower puree and salsa verde piqued my interested the most initially about this pork belly dish. The puree wasn't too noticeable and the salsa verde and rioja jam were used pretty sparingly. Without being said, I thought the porky belly itself was tasty, albeit more the size I think of when I think about a traditional tapa. I probably wouldn't order it again, but I did enjoy it. Third Course- Tarta de Chocolate: Thank goodness this was a small portion. I probably couldn't have eaten much more. The small piece of dark chocolate tart totally hit the spot. It was almost fudge-like. The small piece of orange and pistachio pieces sat adjacently on the other side of my plate and added a nice touch. The tart could have worked well enough on its own. Beverage- Temporada Sangria: This was a white wine sangria which consisted of mango and pomegranate. The pieces of fruit in the cocktail were delightful. This was a sweet drink that could go down way to easily if you aren't careful. It was both light and refreshing. Between the courses I loved and the courses I really enjoyed, I had a really great meal. I was ready to return to Amada before I finished dinner, but I'm really inspired to return after reminiscing about my experience in this review.

text: In the past year a lot has changed at Sabor for Christian Mena and Lino Oliviera, the proprietors of this downtown Edmonton restaurant. Sabor has been renamed and rebranded, their third restaurant Urbano Pizza Co. has opened next door, and Sabor has become 100% Ocean Wise approved. That's a big list of accomplishments for one year, but the Ocean Wise certification is one of the most exciting for their annual seafood festival. I had the pleasure of attending the kick off to this year's Seafood Festival to preview some of Chef Lino's new dishes. The night started off with a bang with the Sabor Caesar Shot: a Malpeque oyster topped with sturgeon caviar and served with a Caesar shot featuring Eau Claire Three Point Vodka. I love that Sabor chose to feature Eau Claire Distillery - as Alberta's first craft distillery, their spirits are sure to impress if you haven't tried them yet! Each table was offered a Pinchos Board, featuring some of the items available on the menu at Bodega Tapas & Wine, to kick off the evening. Pinchos, which are related to tapas, differ such that pinchos are often presented spiked with toothpicks. In Spanish culture, the toothpicks serve as a method of picking up your food, but also as a way to charge you for how much you've eaten. Luckily Sabor doesn't charge based on toothpick count, because I would have had to shell out a lot of money! Our board for the evening featured Sabor's Aceitonas (house marinated olives, $5), octopus and mussel salad ($6, pictured above), crab fritters, seared scallops on pork belly, and snails in red wine with chorizo. The scallops and pork belly were a hit at our table, with the crispy crab fritters a close second. Olives, octopus and snail are such polarizing dishes to begin with, so I found that at our table there was not much in-between, you either liked the dish or you didn't. Our second starter for the evening was Chef Lino's play on Fish and Chips, featuring deep fried lake smelt and piri piri spiced chips. The fish were battered and fried to have a crisp coating, and the piri piri chips had a light seasoning to them. Fair warning though, the lake smelt are deep fried whole, so you chew on the small, edible bones with each bite. Unfortunately the fish and chips are not on the Seafood Festival menu, but Chef Lino will be featuring them once in a while throughout August. Next up was the beautiful Crudo Con Pebre ($24), featuring fresh Red Spring Salmon, Ahi Tuna, BC Coast Halibut, and BC Scallops. The raw seafood was topped with a simple combination of diced tomato, onion, garlic, cilantro, olive oil, and lemon which allowed the natural sweetness of each component to shine through. If you're a sashimi fan, this dish is for you. The following course was a Sardine Flatbread, paying tribute to Urbano Pizza Co. next door. The flatbread was light and covered in a briny onion and anchovy spread that I could not stop eating. Combined with the black olives and portions of sardines, I quite enjoyed this course for the evening. Entrees that evening kicked off with Grilled Humboldt Squid & Prawns ($18) on a bed of chorizo and white bean puree. This squid, otherwise known as the Red Devil, was cooked until soft and very easy to chew. I personally prefer my squid with more bite and chew (like most Asians!), so this dish may not be for everyone. What I really did enjoy though was the bean puree - rich, creamy, and with a kick of heat from the chorizo! Despite having tried a wide variety of tasty seafood dishes, the star of the evening for me was the Bacon Wrapped Sturgeon on Puttanesca Sauce ($32). Sturgeon flesh is quite under-appreciated given that the prized caviar is what most people are after. It was great to see this fish as the star of the plate, and the firmer texture made for a substantial protein.There was smokiness from the bacon, salt and acidity from the sauce, and natural sweetness from the fish to bring everything together. To finish off our family style meal everyone was treated to Mama Margarita's Pudim Flan. This flan is one of Chef Lino's favourite desserts made by his mother, and she finally caved and gave him the recipe. This Portuguese custard is creamy and sweet, and you can taste the richness of the eggs. Word on the street is that this custard is soon to become a gelato flavour at Urbano! While Sabor serves up seafood on their menu throughout the year, the best time to enjoy all that the restaurant has to offer is during the seafood festival. If you can't decide on a specific dish, Chef Lino is also offering off menu family-style dining at $55/person. It's great value and fun for the whole table! The seafood is fresh, the dishes are inventive, and best of all, everything is 100% Ocean Wise. What's stopping you?

The thousand layer bread at Rangoon is one of my favorite things, and I was hoping it would be comparable. On the positive side, it is a better value than at Rangoon, and they give you at least 2x as much of the curry dip all for less money. On the negative side, the roti itself isn't as good as the thousand layer bread. It's a little crispier throughout, and not as buttery. The other negative is that despite being advertised as chicken and potato dip, there was no chicken in the dip. I could see a few little shreds, but no actual pieces. There were several chunks of potato. For less money and a good serving, I can't really complain. For my main, I had the famous beef rendang. The meat itself was exceedingly tender, and the portion size for $15.50 was much better than Rangoon's garbage portion of Pagan beef for $12.50. The sauce itself is a bit dry and doesn't have much flavor to it. It's not bad, but it's just a little bland. I'm not sure how readers of CNN International declared it the most delicious food in the world. My biggest issue, and this seems to be an issue in Chinatown, as it's the 3rd place I've had this sort of issue, is that for $15.50 it doesn't come with rice. I know they offer a smaller portion over rice, but I wanted enough for dinner and leftovers. There's no reason they should charge for a side of rice after paying $15.50. They include some sliced cucumber and what I assume to be carrots and daikon. I have no idea why they give you the start to a banh mi, but they could've left that out and just given me the small side of rice instead. The Malaysian iced tea is fantastic. It tastes like a combination of chocolate milk and Thai tea. The service was a little weird. I was seated immediately, it was relatively late, the restaurant wasn't packed, but it wasn't empty at all. It took me around 10-12 minutes to waive down a waiter to take my order. There were several of them standing around, and the other few served tables around me and didn't seem to notice I wanted to order. The food came out quickly, so I can't complain that much. The other thing that was weird is that my waiter never brought over water, but everyone around me was served water. I had to ask another waiter to bring me a glass. There are some other things I would like to try, so I will be back. The restaurant itself is very nice looking so that's a plus. It has a bit of an odd design.

Drums sound muddled (no punchiness). They usually try to compensate for the terrible echo and lack of clarity by pumping up the juice to a nearly unbearable level. People will still come for the great musical acts that show up (usually at a very reasonable price), so I'm hoping they'll save up enough money to do some serious renovation and acoustic upgrades. text: The approach that I'm going to take with rating the telecom/internet/cable industry is going to be from the ground up. As an industry, they just seem to not really like their customers. All of these companies start at one star and work their way up from there. From the beginning of the business relationship, you are typically given the bait-and-switch - you know, you get your 1 year intro rate, then prices begin to rise significantly. Since that is the standard, a person shopping for internet/phone/cable service then knows that they need to find two prices to do comparison shopping: the intro rate, and the standard rate. The intro rate is easy to find, but you need to be Sherlock Holmes sometimes to find the standard rate - it's exhausting and annoying! Then, to get answers you typically have to go through a call center - yay! Some of these call centers are overseas, and some are in the US. Either way, they are time consuming to have to deal with. Okay, now you're signed into a contract with one of these companies. Well, the service usually rolls without a hitch, but let me relate an experience that I had with Clearwire/Sprint: the service was getting bad and I was experiencing outages. When I'd call for support, they'd hand me to online tech support that seems to work off a queue card and the typical problem that they'd lead you on to would be that if you were using your own router then according to them the problem was the third party router - this was the problem every time! I'd eventually have to suggest that they needed to reset my connection on their switch to resolve the issue - fixed the problem every time. One time the problem was bad and was not getting resolved no matter what they did. We kept going back and forth for a few weeks until my problem was finally escalated to someone that could check the coverage area - it turns out that Sprint/Clearwire was pulling out of my market area and failed to tell me! These companies are so annoying to deal with and not one of them seems to want to break the mold. So here we go for this company... Just dropping this on Clearwire/Sprint (whoever owns it now), since they are the initial source of my disgust with the ISP industry.

My friend and I kept asking each other which the other liked best but we honestly could not decide. Thank God for combo platters! I typically go for the the pulled pork everywhere, but with the chicken so flavorful, the ribs so tender and smokey, and the brisket literally melting in your mouth...I cannot decide. For dessert, Chef Hailey Riley treated us to homemade apple pie served from the oven to the table topped with maple ice cream with nuts. The combination of their apple pie and ice cream was phenomenal! So that is the food portion. Here is a little bit about the staff. They were all fun, entertaining, knowledgeable, and truly a team. Dexter was our main server, but at three other staff members came by to either ask if we needed more water, a drink from the bar, or to clear out empty plates. It was a nice day out and found it odd that they were not seating anyone outside. That was disappointment number one. Second, would be the food. I ordered the wild mushroom flatbread and he ordered the crab cake benedict. The presentation was nice but my friend report the food was boring and the portion unsatisfying. My flatbread was okay but the crust was hard. Perhaps the used the gluten-free bread by mistake. Also the wild mushroom was made up of only one type of mushroom that appeared to be baby bellas. Not very exciting. The most disappointing experience was the drinks. It was brunch so I ordered a mimosa alleges to be made from fresh squeezed orange juice and my friend ordered a Bloody Mary. The orange juice was Tropicana without any pulp (see picture). I mean if you're going to fake fresh squeezed, at least get some OJ with pulp. As for the Bloody Mary, it was boring without fanfare. They offer many options for fixings but the waiter/bartender made no effort to ask. The only positive feedback I can give is that we got two meals and three drinks for less than $50. text: So this place beat out my regular steak house, in a local name the best steakhouse competition a while back. Since the boyfriend had a birthday coming up, which is our excuse to go try fancy steakhouses, we figured we'd try this one out. I mean our regular is delish, so we thought this place must be AWESOME! Disappointedly, it was not. When we arrived, one of the waitresses and a man in a suit who I assumed to be a manager or owner of some sort were standing right beside the door. Neither of them said anything to us, or bothered to open the door for us to go inside. Not a huge biggie but I just thought that a little odd. The Food: I was disappointed in the menu as soon as I had read everything. None of their appetizers seemed like anything out of the ordinary. We had the garlic parm shrimp and the crab bisque. You better REALLY love garlic if you get the shrimp!! I couldn't tell what was garlic and what was cheese on my plate but it all looked and tasted like it was a ton of garlic. The bisque was a tad bit fishy to me and I'm not really into that taste. If I remember correctly the steaks were a little more expensive here than at other places. I got the 8oz. center cut ribeye. There was a little * on the menu saying that all of their steaks would be served with a char. Which a little char is fine, but my steak came out completely black on one end. Otherwise it was cooked medium to my liking. I had to cut off the black though to be able to finish the whole thing. Which I wasn't too crazy about not being able to eat the whole thing since I was paying so much for it. Their side item selection was lacking. I mean who doesn't have scalloped potatoes or mashed potatoes?? Instead they've got steak fries, which look exactly what a gas station would call a tator log. Tator logs are not my idea of fine dining. I ordered the loaded baked potato. It was ok but something I couldn't place was lacking from it making it a little bland despite all the toppings. We also had a piece of cheesecake for desert. It was SO GOOD. However, it wasn't made in house. :( It was imported from New York. The Waiter and Amosphere: Our waiter was nice enough. They make them wear these goofy fake sport coats. They hang a little loose on all of them and are terrible shade of tan. Our waiter was sweating like a mad man. He did a great job up until we were done eating our steaks. Then he just sort of disappeared for a while, showed back up to ask if we wanted desert, and then never reappeared again until time for the check. We could have used a refill before dessert. The atmosphere in here is nice though. Dark and dimly lit as you would expect. Wine cabinets with nice lighting shining on them. There was a girl there singing and playing the piano, so that was kind of nice. She wasn't too loud, so we could still hear each other talk and not have to compete with her. It looked like they may have even had a seating area out back, but no one was seated there, so it could have just been a wait area. In closing, I felt like they maybe didn't have a professionally trained chef in this restaurant. Nothing on the menu seemed out of the box and there were no daily special or soup of the day or anything. The staff was nice but didn't really go out of their way to show their appreciation. In other places I have been, the manager or owner comes around after dinner to ask how me the meal was and thank you for your business. This did not happen here. Our waiter barely even came back to our table after our main coarse was finished. Anyway, I think we'll just stick to what we know is good next time and return to our regular Mr. John's Steakhouse.
label: NEG

That's how long I had to wait... in order to wait in line, get a number, wait some more, talk to an agent for 8 minutes, have my paperwork and eyesight approved (they screwed up my vision assessment -- unless I am to believe them over my Vandy eye doctor), be told that my registration is set, and walk out the door. Go to the next and find the sweetest candy ever. Eat lots of rice? Buy it by the burlap sack. Don't have pots or plates? They have high quality selections. Want to steam some dumplings you bought here? Get a cheap bamboo steamer before you leave. Don't forget to pick up and fresh bahn mi at the far end. Also check out the other baked goods, frozen proteins and dim sum. Really kind service from the check out folks. When leaving, you can also buy beautiful bamboo shoot, and even DVDs. It's crazy the collection of items they have. And everything is great. Ok, so while it isn't a glitzy place, not recently renovated, who really cares? What's really cool is you can spend a whole day here, getting a haircut, massage, getting tax work done, enjoying coffee, and even sitting at restaurant. text: Never have I experienced service that made me as uncomfortable as I was in Ocean Harbor. Granted, I dined here at an odd hour--around 9pm, but the place is open until 11pm!!! Dim sum hours were over, but made to order dinner was still going on. The place was empty, except for 2-3 tables still eating. This is my first time here, so I took a while to figure out what to order. The staff seemed a bit impatient and began talking smack about my table in Chinese. I don't understand Chinese, but I believe I am socially capable enough to pick up on the non-verbal cues they were shooting our way. We hastily ordered salted baked squid, baked chicken and clams with black beans sauce. Even though I was starving, I still thought the food was mediocre. The squid was simply rolled in dough and fried to a crisp, which was the most edible plate. The baked chicken was soaked in fat, what's the point of it being baked anymore? The clams were poorly cleaned and the sauce was way too salty. My dining companion ordered a side of hot and sour soup, but spat it out after the first taste because it was rotten. I didn't believe him so I tried it myself and I was shocked at how disgusting it tasted. Just imagine leaving a bowl of soup out for a week and let it spoil...that's what they fed us. The one waiter noticed how dissatisfied we were with our food, so he brought out complimentary bean soup desserts. Still, that can't make up for our horrendous experience here. We quickly paid and ran out, vowing never to lay eyes on this place ever again.
label: NEG

text: I had a very disappointing experience at Puckett's, especially after reading all of the excellent reviews. The Mule arrived in a mason jar as opposed to the traditional copper plated mug and, more importantly, contained no ginger beer or lime. Instead it was a sour concoction of seltzer, grapefruit juice, and (possibly) gin. The TN Arnold Palmer was at least palatable, but heavily watered down. - Food was mediocre at best. We ordered the Country Club and the Piggy Mac. The Country Club was practically inedible. My fiancee ate only three bites before putting it down. Tough chicken, oversalted ham, and wilted lettuce. Hubby tried the brunch option SEC (Sausage Egg Cheese) burrito, which he said was good. The "hash browns" were not hash browns so much as American fries, slightly undercooked. Beer selection is okay - they have a varied group to select from and we usually find a beer or two we like. It would be awesome if they had a beer menu printed that had more descriptions of each beer. On previous visits we have had their standards sandwiches - I have had the veggie and hubby has had the Reuben, which were fairly decent to good - you figured they were providing food for an option to go with the beer, not as a "foodie" kind of joint, so the food met expectations. But if they are going to advertise themselves as a lunch and brunch joint, they really either need to go all out and be good at doing the food or just be a really good, solid beer place with just a few GOOD food options that are there to soak up the beer. If they are going to do the latter, then amp up the beer selection, and just have food as a side to the beer. If they want to be known for lunch/brunch, they really need to get GOOD at the food side and have quality food with some good beer options that pair nicely with the food. text: 5 of us including 2 kids arrived about 6:00 on a Saturday. The main parking lot was already full but plenty of parking on other side. However, some of those must have been employee's cars as there weren't quite that many diners inside. The decor is welcoming, very nice, looks and feels Thai. 5 stars for Thai ambiance. We were seated right away and several other groups came in as we looked over the menus. We had printed out some coupons from their website but forgot them at home. I pulled up the coupon on my phone and before we ordered anything we explained we had forgot the hard copies. The waitress said we could not use that, they had to be printed out. It's 2015, imo, showing your phone should be acceptable now. Also, NO kids menu which is very disappointing so plan on spending adult prices for your kids meals. 5 Thai teas, Crab Rangoon and Spring Rolls to start. Thai tea is so good and addicting as it should be. Rangoon was made with curry powder which I hadn't had before, it was different, and good. The (2) Spring Rolls were standard fare. Being our first visit there, and one of our groups 1st Thai experience ever, we both ordered Pad Thai. I know it's Thai version 1.0 but I like it. Their Pad Thai comes with 2 shrimp and chicken. It was quite good. I would say that the sauce however did not have quite as much flavor as others I've had. I've seen this before with Pad Thai, it seems the lighter the color, the less flavor. It's not a spice/heat issue either so maybe it's the ratio of fish sauce or tamarind? It was still good and I would get it again. My newbie decided to kick it up a notch with the spice tray and she liked it. The wife got the Amazing, a peanut sauce dish which was quite different than the "Amazing" she gets at our usual Thai place. Not what she expected, she really liked it and would get it again. It was quite spicy though which was not indicated as such on the menu. One of the kids ordered their usual sushi rolls which they said were really good, but not quite as good as they had at Jimmy's last week. The other ordered the Broccoli entree with Chicken. That dish was made with Royal Oyster sauce and we asked for it on the side, we also asked to substitute baby corn for carrots, all of which came out as requested. The broccoli was cooked perfectly with good flavor, and the kid even dipped the chicken in the oyster sauce which was also very good. I would totally order that dish for myself next time. Being a party of 5 they automatically add 18% gratuity to the check which totaled $106. That may sound expensive but we didnt order any expensive dishes. It adds up though, Thai teas are $3.00 each, we ordered 2 appetizers, and 2 sushi rolls, and one kid who we can normally feed for $5-6 had to order an $11 adult meal. Overall the atmosphere, food and portions were very good, the service was decent, and it was a nice dining experience. We will go back. 4 stars is my highest rating for a restaurant like this as I reserve my 5th star for rare incredible experiences and/or very high end establishments.

text: THE SHORT STORY: People with food allergies should AVOID this restaurant! The owner, kitchen staff, and servers do not have thorough knowledge of the ingredients, and do not take responsibility for related mistakes. THE LONG STORY: For context - I have a delayed anaphylactic reaction to pine nuts. It is the same reaction as people who have to use an EpiPen and rush to the ER, except that my throat swells shut more gradually. That means that I have time to take Benadryl orally and avoid the ER (and death) as long as I get it into my system quickly enough. It is still a miserable aftermath, but death is avoidable and often so is the ER, so I consider myself lucky. ... I was in Santa Barbara visiting with friends on Labor Day weekend, and we had dinner at Blue Agave. I am diligent about reading ingredients and asking about pine nuts at restaurants, however some food types are pretty universally pine nut free (Mexican, Thai, Indian...). At Blue Agave, I did not ask before ordering since Mexican is on my safe to eat list. After eating a bite of the meal, my mouth felt itchy, and I immediately flagged down the waitress. She assured me, and then checked with the kitchen staff and REassured me, that there were no pine nuts in their kitchen let alone my meal. I have many mild allergies as well, so I continued to have a few more bites. My reaction got worse, so I stopped eating and took the Benadryl that I had with me. Unfortunately, I was in the bathroom vomiting soon after. It became pretty clear that I would need to get more Benadryl and head back to the hotel. I stopped the waitress on my way out and told her that despite what she had been informed by the kitchen staff, there definitely were pine nuts in my meal, and to be aware of that if someone asked in the future. At that point, the owner, Brad Sherman approached us. He introduced himself and reiterated that there were absolutely no pine nuts in their food. (That made three separate, matter of fact assurances that despite my reaction, I had not ingested pine nuts). I asked him for a list of ingredients, because if indeed there were no pine nuts, I would need to be tested for a new severe allergy. He was able to give me a list of ingredients in the rice (which I had wrongly suspected might be the culprit), but was only able to tell me that there were many ingredients in the Mole and he could not provide me with a list. He agreed to email me a complete list. A week later (I will say a week for the sake of simplicity, though I did not actually receive an email for an additional week, and only after I reached out to him), Mr. Sherman informed me via email that there were in fact crushed up pine nuts in the mole. He apologized, and said that he had trusted the kitchen staff when they told him there weren't any. (I will say that I understand that this happens, and I appreciated his honesty, which I told him.). Mr. Sherman changed his tone when my husband asked him to refund our meals ($120 for food that neither of us was able to eat on account of my reaction to the pine nuts). We would never have asked for a refund if the waitress had informed me correctly about the pine nuts when I asked after the first bite. In his email to my husband, Mr. Sherman wrote: "I am very sorry your night was curtailed, and if it was our fault I would quickly refund that payment. However, since this clearly was not a problem emanating on the part of our staff, I do not think that a refund is in order. " ...Since I had not asked about pine nuts before ordering, the owner of the restaurant dismissed any responsibility on the part of the staff - even though they admittedly were not aware of the pine nuts and would have served them to me anyway. I emailed Mr. Sherman one more time, reiterating the request for a refund since my not asking before ordering clearly would not have have made a difference. That was five days ago and I have not gotten any response. It was my experience that Mr. Sherman's approach to the restaurant business is reckless. Had I not recognized my allergic reaction despite him personally misinforming me about the ingredients, I would have died and he would be dealing with my family right now (who lost my mother to this same exact allergic reaction 25 years ago) instead of me. In dismissing any fault where clearly there was much, Mr. Sherman has demonstrated extremely poor business practice. There is also great cause for concern for people with allergies, because if he truly does not believe that he is responsible for misinforming me about the ingredients, then there is no reason to think that he will implement strategies for avoiding such mistakes in the future. Steer clear of Blue Agave if you have food allergies, or even if you are just a person who chooses to support honest business practices.

text: I was so disappointed with the service at this restaurant today. It was obvious that the place was busy, but as out-of-towners I could only assume that this was the norm and that the knew what they were doing. Obviously, that was not the case. With two small children in tow, we waited over an hour and a half from the time we walked into the place, an hour of that being time between ordering and receiving our food. No one kept us updated on timing, notified us of any delays at all, or checked in. When my husband finally flagged someone down to ask about the delay, our server gave no apology and instead said, "other people got here first." WHAT?! Obviously they were busy, but it would have been simple at that point to say, "wow, sorry about that, we're totally understaffed today." Instead the response was downright rude. I was so annoyed (and hangry!) that I straight out told our server that if she would just apologize for the 1 hour delay on food, it wouldn't be as big a deal, which she did grudgingly. As we left the restaurant, I stopped to speak to the manager. I explained in less than 2 minutes of talk time (as opposed to a "twenty minute rant" as the business owner's yelp response claimed) that we had a really bad experience, that we waited for over an hour, that our kids were hungry, and that their wait staff was unapologetic. At NO POINT during that talk did I say that anyone was awful, make any personal attacks, or exaggerations. I simply stated what had happened, said that an apology would have fixed it, and explained that I was saying this so that they would have the opportunity to fix this problem for other guests in the future. The manager I spoke with was understanding and apologetic, and seemed reasonable about it all. I thought we might have just had a fluke of a bad experience, but the fact that the business owner went on yelp to accuse me on my husband Bill K's post that I was "ranting in front of my child" is rude, unnecessary, and factually incorrect. Telling people in a straightforward way about a problem and how they could fix it, without personal attacks, is not a "rant," nor is it something that should be hidden from children (my personal argument is that it's good to teach kids to advocate for themselves within reason, but that's my own personal view). And, side note, "never seen a rant like this before"???!! You have led a truly charmed life as a restaurant owner. Congratulations, owner/yelper of The Mex Authentic - not only did you ruin my lunch, now you've ruined my day by calling me out personally as some kind of crazy lady and inspiring me to write a bad review (which, as is obvious in my yelp profile, I rarely do!). What poor management of a business, when it would have been so easy to just say "we're sorry" and move on. UPDATE: In response to the owner's comment below, I just want to clarify that an apology sounds like this, "I'm sorry." It doesn't sound like a passive-aggressive list of personal attacks and excuses, followed by "I wish you well." Furthermore, there was absolutely no apology for the personal attack in your response to my husband's post claiming that I went on a "twenty minute rant against your manager without giving him time to get a word in." Wishing me well doesn't change that that was a histrionic exaggeration that deserves an apology in and of itself. I am not a difficult customer - I made no special requests, I communicated my valid feelings and experiences without exaggeration or personal attacks, and yet you have represented your business by going on the web to do both. I guess all I have to say is . . . I wish you well.

text: OK, so I've read the other reviews of this Trader Joe's and I am ready to weigh in. So, I have waited 9 years, 7 months and 2 days for Boise to get a Trader Joe's. I wrote letters faithfully every couple of months for all that time and was estatic when I heard it was opening. I lived in San Francisco for 12 years and fell in love with it there. I could go on about all the great stuff they have, but other folks have already done that. What I want to address are the haters who are writting negative reviews. 1st, yes the parking lot is not the best, I go around 10 in the morning and there is NOBODY there, I can park right in front of the store, no problem. I think it doesn't get nasty until after noon or so. I realize that many folks can't shop until after work, BUT, there is a parking garage RIGHT ACROSS THE STREET at BODO. They will carry your groceries to that parking garage and any other for you if you need help, no problem. I have gotten discount coupons for the parking garage also from the front desk when I parked there, you might just have to ask. 2nd, To complain that you have to drive all the way downtown is total crap, seriously, people in the Treasure Valley have no perspective about what real traffic is like or how far one has to drive in larger urban areas. I live in Meridian and it takes me a grand total of 13 mins door to door, big deal. I heard someone complain that they had to drive all the way from Eagle. Really?! If you live in Eagle I'm pretty sure you are use to having to drive a long way for ANYTHING. People, you are spoiled here, and good luck finding organic/non-GMO food for the prices they have at Trader's. I think your savings would off set the price of fuel, which some yelpers complained about. 3rd, I have never had bad service here, on the contrary, the crew members are very helpful and very friendly. To address the complaints that they are always stocking and there are boxes stacked around, I wonder if you have ever been to another Traders because that is the norm, as they want to keep everything as well stocked as they can. This is to deal with all of those who complain if something isn't in stock. I have never had any trouble getting around these, and every other grocer in this town stocks as well, with plenty of boxes to navigate around also. 4th, no, you can't find absolutely everything on your list at Trader's. They carry around 3,000 products. Normal grocery stores can carry up to 50,000. But, what you can get is exceptional, and if you don't like anything for any reason, they will give you your money back if you return the packaging, even if you eat every last bite. In a nutshell, be freakin' happy we finally have a Trader Joe's here and stop complaining about everything.

text: I chose Taste of the World based on the glowing reviews I read here on Yelp. It ended up being a terrible mistake and below is a detailed review of our evening. We were told to sit anywhere by said server since there is no host/hostess. We chose to sit outside since there were ZERO customers inside and it was a nice night. After ten minutes we were handed menus printed on plain office paper. We leafed through the rather uninteresting menu and decided to try the mushroom and goat cheese strudel as an appetizer. For our main course, my wife chose the Filet and I decided to try the Paella. The owner stopped by and i mentioned my affinity fkr paella. He told me it was the chef's special spin on Mexican paella. Which falsely raised my expectatiins. About 25 minutes after we ordered, the strudel showed up and it and was phenomenal. Immediately our mood improved in hopes the main course would be just as good and we could ignre the dismally slow service. Unfortunately, it only got worse. My wife's risotto was flavorless and her steak was chewy and just as bland. My paella...I have to say it was the single worst dish I have ever been served. The rice was so undercooked it wasn't edible. The chirozo was as dry as saw dust. The chicken was chewy and I literally couldn't swallow my first (and only) bite. Finally, the seafood. To my dismay, this was the worst part of the dish. The shrimp and calamari seemed to have been boiled for 30+ minutes and were completely flavorless. The final straw ended with a muscle that was so foul I had to use my napkin, again, or risk getting sick from eating bad seafood. And while our server removed the Paella from our check and gave his apologies the owner was no where to be found. I cannot express how awkward this entire experience was. Our night was literally ruined and I will never go back. Although I wanted to be as pleased with this establishment as others, it fell flat in every single category. If you're looking for great atmosphere and a fun night out, stick to Main.

text: After seeing this place listed as the best restaurant in Nashville on TripAdvisor (right behind a pizza place and coffee shop), we made reservations the day of (Friday night) through Open Table while traveling. We enjoyed the high-end feel, and my fiancé wore a polo, jeans, and tennis shoes, so it wasn't pretentious. The wait staff was kind and knowledgeable about the food and wine list in great detail and offered amazing recommendations for both! The food was superb: - Pork belly appetizer was so tender it could easily be cut with a fork and melted in your mouth! - The filet mignon was tender (even at medium well) and had amazing, juicy flavors. I'm a steak snob after living in Dallas for years, so I was impressed with this steak! - The fried brussel sprouts side is the way to go if you love brussel sprouts at all! They taste succulent, but without a bunch of fried breading. All sides are meant to be shared with 1-2 other people. The two of us shared one side. We enjoyed the wine recommended to us and appreciated the fact that our waitress suggested a good-priced wine, not the expensive ones. Cabernet bottle prices start at $60-70 a bottle and run much higher! For one appetizer, two meals, one side, and a bottle of wine, we spent $180 before tip. The average dinner plate runs $30, which is a great price for what you get and being so high rated...filets are easily $50 at other steak houses! I highly recommend to anyone staying close to downtown Nashville. It's also a street over from Music Row and all of the action!

text: I hate to be negative about this place because it would be a bit unfair. It is what it is and doesn't try to be something that its not....Except for the name of the place. It really is "Just a place to stay". I wanted to write this review so others would know and not get their hopes up. I thought the woman who worked there was nice. She let me check in early, and they really do mean well. But to be fair to everyone...this place isn't for everyone. We'll start with the fact that it's old and looked like a house that was converted into a "Hotel". With two large doors to enter, a delayed doorbell just to enter and four floors to walk without an elevator, be prepared and don't pack heavy stuff. My room was really two separate rooms from some time ago that shared a small bathroom. The rooms were small with noticeable wear, mainly no switch plates on an electrical outlet, window-mounted AC units and a sink that was pulled forward from the wall. The furniture was in good shape for it's age and a curious small corner closet would not open because the knob was missing (go figure). The room did have a flat-screen TV but it has the most basic cable ever. When I did locate the second remote, I could watch a little TV. I had a traditional key that opened my door as well as the front door, which is locked after 8 PM. OK.....Downstairs is The Monkey Bar, A nice enough corner bar with character. Seems like a nice place....for a 20-something to hang out in. Again I hate to bash this place because I do think they mean well, but "It's Not a Hotel....It's really a Bed and Breakfast....Minus the Breakfast". I was told there was no breakfast, but that there would be coffee with some pastries. I'm sure they were there because the day's table setting had them. There's free WiFi which was cool. The small shower was big enough with good water pressure. I had a small, dorm room-type refrigerator which I kept my free water and Dr. Pepper sodas. Even had a leftover of each from the previous person. The bed was comfortable enough and there was an iron and ironing board. I had towels which were fresh and shampoo and conditioner but no soap. Overall the place served its purpose for me, but it's not really for me. Costs a bit too much and is what it is and doesn't apologize for that. Again, don't mean to be negative, just need to people to be aware when considering this spot. It's just not gonna be for everyone.

text: It is with enthusiasm that I endorse Bluedeer Yoga studio. As a practitioner of Bikram Yoga for over 20 years, I have found myself very discouraged these past 5-8 years. I even left the practice to try other yogas, such as Ashtanga and Vinyasa. But I missed the heat and the flexibility it afforded me. I am happy to report I have found my yoga home at Bluedeer Yoga. It offers Core courses, created by Tony Sanchez, which are similar to Bikram but saner. For example, the minor grip changes, and focus on straightening the leg versus locking the knee, are subtle but profound. Suzanne, the owner, and former teacher of Bikram (indeed, one of my earliest instructors) is masterful in her nuanced and precise instruction. For her, it's all about alignment and not muscling into a posture too soon. Other instructor Ruth, also knowledgable, brings humor to the class. The studio is lovely, light, roomy, and best of all, no stinky carpet! If you are looking for a solid yoga practice, with excellent instruction, Bluedeer is for you

text: I've always been a little wary of restaurant week. My inner cheapskate breaks down the numbers of the restaurants offering everything from special dishes to old favorites to one-off dessert experiments, and weighs this with my typical levels of hunger. Most often, the result is a decisive Nahh, I'll just wait for the crowds to die down and order the exact amount of food I want for the price I expect/am willing to pay. That said, when I saw that East Passyunk Avenue, Philly's hottest nook of up-and-coming dining spots, was hosting their own neighborhood restaurant week, I immediately raced over to OpenTable to make a reservation for my two girlfriends and I. I gotta say that, while I was A-OK with the mandatory phone-in reservation at Zahav a few weeks ago, there's a remarkable ease and convenience to being able to filter using number of diners, date, and time when we were looking for a Monday night out on the town. We spotted space at Townsend and booked it post-haste. We made the right choice. Since there were three of us, we figured we'd try one of each course. Then we saw that one of the first courses was a foie gras butternut squash terrine. And since I'd just binged on terrines last week.... looks like we're doubling up on Brandades! Course one (served shortly after a DIVINE bread basket [that may have been divine or may have merely been 'good', we were pretty hungry]) included a creamy parsnip veloute with brown butter chestnuts, a hint of black truffle, and just enough brussels sprout leaves to leave us wanting more (hee hee). The brandade, a dish I'd never had before, was a crunchy brioche topped with a quail egg, shellfish bouillabaisse, and pernod. How such a tiny little toasty brioche could be so full of flavor.... well I don't (per)nod, but it was incredible. The veloute was rich and creamy, a nice complement to the light fluff and crunch of the other appetizer. But the best was yet to come... I'll shoot you straight, the pasta/vegetarian dish was a little cold by the time it got to us. Flavor-wise, it was fairly unremarkable, and the tastes of caramelized onions and fennel, while there, were hints. If you were only getting this dish, I would not consider your experience worthwhile. BUT if you're lucky enough to have some dining pals, perhaps they'll slip you bites of the glorious speck-wrapped cod (bottom right) atop Tarbais bean garbure with tiny cockles (that came with their own fork!) This fish fell apart the moment your fork touched it, delicate... dare I say exquisite? Oh, if I dared, I'll repeat that word for the venison en crepinette (different from the online menu, description here). Exquisite. We nearly came to (fork) blows over these half-dollar sized medallions, each soaking up the jus and pairing perfectly with the parsnip pureé. This dish would bring me back again and again. Somehow, we had room for dessert. Luckily, it was both light and a delight. The crème brûlée, flawless. Visible vanilla bean is my jam. The blue cheese plate was a nice tangy option for those without a sweet tooth. And for those WITH a sweet tooth: enter pavlova. No, she's not your exotic, sexy neighbor (maybe she is, I don't know where you live). She is actually an it, specifically a crunchy meringue dish topped with mixed berries and strawberry coulis, speckled with fresh mint. Yup. Imagine the finest cotton candy you can even fathom. And then make it fancy, and French, and bury it in berries. We couldn't get enough. Take your dates, your dads, your dudes, your dames, yourself, take them all to Townsend. I'll be back soon to try out their take on rabbit.... I've only heard (read* since I practically live on Yelp) the best things. Thanks, Tod and team, for the tasty treats.

text: My review is long, but worth the read, I feel. In the two years attended this school, I have been subject to instructors constantly reading from the book, or being subject to sit through hours worth of PowerPoint presentations. I have also had to fight tooth and nail, over a six month ordeal, to get a grade corrected, when an instructor didn't give me a grade for a project I emailed to him on the date it was due. This was, of course after having my emails ignored by the program chair, the dean of my program, and the instructor himself, as well as being told by the director of the school that I should be glad I didn't get an 'F' as a final grade. This school is also chock FULL of people of questionable character. Many of the students LOOK like they're on drugs much of the time, some of them SMELL of drugs, and several will ADMIT to being high in class every week. Not only that, but the level of morality that people here have is often very low. For instance, several students have had their laptops stolen, when their backs were turned, right out of their bags or off the table. Then, you have the issue with having to go in and have your schedule corrected each quarter, when you're not a full-time student, yet they sign you up as one each new quarter, but state that the system only shows you part-time, and should only schedule you as such. Lets also not forget about the BLATANT, and FLAT-OUT lies they will tell you to hook you into attending. I was told by my recruiter that credits transfer very easily, that you can test out of up to 50% of the classes in the NSA program, and that, if necessary, the school understands when you need to miss class for a week or so, due to life's events. All of these were false informations! ITT is only nationally accredited, which means that any other school, such as IUPUI, which is both nationally and locally credited, will not accept your credits. It turns out that there are very few school that will, period. You cannot test out of up to 50% of the classes in the NSA program, because you cannot test out of their made-up classes, like "Stategies for the Technical Professional," which is a course on MS Office, and you can't test out of core classes. You CAN test out of General Educations courses, like Math and Composition, but there are only a few of these in the program. The test out program is very rigged as well, so as to keep you from testing out when you've missed the small test out window. Credits WILL transfer in pretty easily, although sometimes you have to fight them to accept them. The school is also NOT very forgiving when missing class. First of all, if you don't inform the instructor that you're missing class, the school will call you to ask why you weren't there, because attendance is taken for each class. Also, most classes have "Lab Time," whether the class really has any labs or not, and your grade for those is often only given by showing up for class, with no way to make it up for missing. Some instructors will just simply not allow you to make up work, either, regardless of why you missed or whether you planned it with them ahead of time. So, often, if you miss a class, you're receiving zeros in the grade book, which most of the time can't be redeemed. One of the most dubious things they've done in the past couple years is to inject an extra course into the curriculum, after we had already signed up, and are most of the way through our degree program. We now must take "Advanced Strategies for the Technical Professional," which includes most of the topics covered in other classes. So, this class is actually just a redundancy, which we all (we students) feel is a money ploy, since we will have to pay for that class. The information from an instructor is that this extra class was included so that military students, who have their tuition paid for by the government, can be considered at least 3/4-time for the duration of their degree, as the government does not pay when they don't got at least 3/4-time. The way it originally worked out is that the last quarter of the degree would only be one class a week, which is only 4.5 credit hours, and drops the government assistance for that quarter. So, it really is just a way for the school to rake in the money. In all, I implore you to FIND A BETTER SCHOOL TO GIVE YOUR MONEY TO!!!

Service was quick, the family running the show was friendly. The daughter was working the ovens, the mother was commanding the register and Joey was running the cold side. It was a very well oiled machine. All in all I plan on returning to Joeys for a slice of cheese pizza in the very near future. That being said, my only complaint and the only thing that prevents a 5 star review is the system they have in place for claiming your order. They have an intercom set up and the expo gal will call out the orders over the speakers when they are ready. The problem is that she just calls out vague things like "two slices of cheese pizza" or "slice of pepperoni." Obviously, this is an issue because there are often many similar orders in the dining room and this creates confusion for the guest. I don't think it's entirely too far fetched to arrange a numbered order system to eliminate uncertainty when you go to claim your slice. At any rate, Joeys, I will be back. You are a pleasant establishment in an unexpected location and I appreciate your diligent efforts to produce NY Style all the way down in Nashville.

text: We decided to stay here to save money... You definitely get what you pay for.
