And though the whole hotel claims to have three cots, all three were "taken" for the duration of our stay. -They claim to have laundry facilities, all of which were outside and most of which were out of order. -Each time any of us went downstairs, there was only one person working, regardless of how many people were waiting. Phones ringing like crazy, two or three people in line, you get the idea. Waited 15mins just to check in. -The surrounding area is extremely... Poor. Closest grocery is Sav-A-Lot and has very limited selections. - The day we checked out, we noticed a "Crime Scene Clean-Up" van with people in clean-suits in and out of a room below us.. Still unsure of what happened there... - The free WiFi never worked. It was an available network, but out of the four of us, not one could get it to work. I've already been promised that next time we go, we will stay somewhere downtown. Transportation across the river is neither cheap nor convenient. (Even the ferry is $2 per person, per trip, with limited hours. When it's up and running.) The difference in what you would pay for the room across the river and what it will cost you to get there from here is pretty negligible. text: My boyfriend and I came here last Friday specifically to try their ramen as I heard they're now selling ramen during their weekday lunch hours. We arrived at 11:15am only to find that they don't open until 11:30. Not a problem. We darted over to Cob's Bakery a couple doors down to grab some baked goods while we waited. When we walked into the establishment, it was FREEZING!! Sooooo sooo cold with the A/C blasting. I'm thankful I had a jean jacket but still.... I couldn't get warm. I was so cold I asked for hot water as my beverage. There was another guest who arrived at the same time as us, and he actually left the restaurant to go to his car and came back with his winter jacket! Lol. Anyways, they serve a several varieties of ramen ranging from $11 - $12. Shio (salt); Shoyu (soy sauce); Miso (soybean paste); Tonkatsu (pork bone broth); and Tan Tan (spicy sesame minced pork). I opted for the Miso bowl while my boyfriend chose the Tonkatsu. The bowls arrived after several minutes piping hot. Eagerly antcipating my first bite, I found it quite disappointing.The broth was overly salty and lacked depth. There were lots of noodles - almost too much compared to the toppings received. I opted to not get the bamboo shoots or fungus added to mine (since I dislike either); and was left with a very bland looking bowl topped with green onion, bits of corn, bean sprouts, some seaweed, and ONE piece of char siu. The ONE piece of pork I received was soooo fatty that by the time I removed the layers of fat, I was left with a nickel size piece of meat *tear*. Oh well, the char siu itself also lacked any identifiable flavour. As for the Tonkatsu my boyfriend ordered, it wasn't much better. The broth lacked the umami and depth it should have and he also found the portion of noodles too much (he couldn't even finish). Overall, a disappointing ramen experience despite having high hopes! I look forward to a real good ramen place in Edmonton.
label: NEG

text: Definitely worth checking out, but make a reservation, because it gets busy! We made 8 p.m. reservations for a Friday. It was about 7:15 p.m. and they said although they might not be able to seat us right away it wouldn't take long. Luckily they were able to seat us right away, but when we left there were a good number of people waiting! Even though there was a lot of times open on opentable, it is misleading, because this is a popular place! Cesare himself was checking people in. It is a really nice touch to have the owner walking around working in the restaurant. It gives it a great family feel. I appreciate how laid back the atmosphere is. We sat outside and the tables were pretty bare without table cloth. When you're covered in sun screen and have sand everywhere, you appreciate not being surrounded by finery. They bring out warm bread with pesto to start. It was good and it helps tide over ravenous beach goers like ourselves. I looked over the menu before we came, and I'm glad I did, because there are so many options. My husband did not, so I had to wait for him to read through everything. I knew I wanted to try the pasta, because it is homemade. My husband chose one dish, but when he heard the specials he decided on the chicken parmesan. I decided on the ravioli with crabmeat and ricotta. The dishes came in a good amount of time. I loved my ravioli. The pink sauce was amazing and I stole some of my husband's pasta to dip in it. I could definitely tell that the ravioli was homemade. The chicken parmesan was good too. It wasn't the best we ever had, but it was pretty good. I bet if we both stuck with just pasta dishes I would have given this place 5 stars. If you are at Clearwater Beach you should come here. Yes it is a little off the beaten path, but that also means there is an abundance of free parking on the side streets. Definitely check this place out.
